d: Israel’s election has left the country facing a political deadlock. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc has won 53 seats, while the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot has 48. With 19 seats held by Arab parties, neither side has secured the 61 seats needed for a majority. Netanyahu has reportedly not ruled out a unity government with Eisenkot, even one involving a rotating prime ministership. Meanwhile, Eisenkot is exploring possible support from Arab parties and ultra-Orthodox factions. What are the options before both leaders, and can Israel avoid another election?
